votes.motion: Approve the earth removal permit for 780 Northfield Road
votes.quote: member alonzo moved to approve the earth removal permit as described at 780 northfield road. seconded by vice chair lehtinen. call for the vote: five-aye. the motion passed unanimously (5-0-0).

votes.motion: Authorize the Town Manager to proceed with the license agreement with Town Counsel for the Food Pantry property at 30 School Street
votes.quote: member alonzo moved to authorize the town manager to proceed with the license agreement with town counsel for the property at 30 school street. seconded by vice chair lehtinen. call for the vote: five-aye. the motion passed unanimously (5-0-0).

votes.motion: Waive building, wiring, plumbing, gas, sheet metal, and technology fees for the Lunenburg Food Pantry project at 30 School Street
votes.quote: member mcquaid moved to waive the building, wiring, plumbing, gas, sheet metal, and technology fees associated with the lunenburg food pantry project at 30 school street. seconded by vice chair lehtinen. call for the vote: five-aye. the motion passed unanimously (5-0-0).

votes.motion: Refer Special Town Meeting articles on Corrective Zoning Amendments and Stormwater Management Bylaw Fee Structure to the Planning Board for review and public hearing
votes.quote: member alonzo moved to refer the special town meeting articles titled "corrective zoning amendments" and "stormwater management bylaw fee structure" to the planning board for review and public hearing. seconded by member mcquaid. call for the vote: five-aye. the motion passed unanimously (5-0-0).

votes.motion: Accept donations for the Town Hall boulder project from Robert Proctor Excavating, Leominster Monument Company, and Lakeview Landscaping
votes.quote: member mcquaid moved to accept the three donations for the town hall boulder project: the boulder from robert proctor excavating, engraving from leominster monument company, and installation/site coordination from lakeview landscaping. seconded by member alonzo. call for the vote: five-aye. the motion passed unanimously (5-0-0).

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of November 13, 2024, March 18, 2025, and April 22, 2025
votes.quote: vice chair lehtinen moved to approve the minutes of november 13, 2024, march 18, 2025, and april 22, 2025. seconded by member alonzo. call for the vote: four-aye. one-abstain (member mcquaid) the motion passed (4-0-1).

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of September 9, 2025; September 15, 2025; October 7, 2025; October 14, 2025; October 21, 2025; and November 17, 2025
votes.quote: chair emkey moved to approve the minutes of september 9, 2025; september 15, 2025; october 7, 2025; october 14, 2025; october 21, 2025; and november 17, 2025. seconded by vice chair lehtinen. call for the vote: three-aye. two-abstain (members alonzo and mcquaid) the motion passed (3-0-2).
vice chair lehtinen moved to adjourn at 9:19 pm. seconded by clerk mcleod. call for the vote: five-aye. the motion passed unanimously (5-0-0).

decisions.decision: Board agreed to review the Boards, Committees, and Commissions Handbook in sections, beginning with Chapters 1 through 6, and to reserve the remote participation chapter for later discussion
decisions.quote: the board agreed to review the document in sections, beginning with chapters 1 through 6, and to reserve the remote participation chapter for later discussion

decisions.decision: Staff directed to research the number, age, and condition of existing AEDs and the cost of replacement, and to review Narcan supplies and expiration dates, with report for future vote
decisions.quote: members supported researching the number, age, and condition of existing aeds and the cost of replacement. member alonzo also suggested reviewing narcan supplies and expiration dates. staff was asked to return with additional information for a future vote.

decisions.decision: Board discussed expectation that Food Pantry continue working toward a permanent location with term of license agreement longer than one year
decisions.quote: the board discussed the need for a term longer than one year and the expectation that the food pantry continue working toward a permanent location.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Board discussed using opioid settlement funds for automated external defibrillator replacements in town and school buildings and police and fire vehicles with preliminary discussion of six-figure total cost

public_comment.speaker: Anthony Sculimbrene
public_comment.stated_role: private citizen, Chair of Architectural Preservation District Commission, Vice Chair of Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee
public_comment.topic: Food Pantry structure classification and building type determination
public_comment.quote: he stated that the building commissioner had classified the structure proposed at 30 school street for the lunenburg food pantry as a permanent building. he disagreed with that classification based on the planning board notice describing a temporary relocation, opengov documents describing the structure as a trailer, and the fact that the structure would be leased.

public_comment.speaker: John Bowen
public_comment.topic: Special Town Meeting procedures and two-thirds vote requirement for transfers
public_comment.quote: he stated that section 81-9 of the town bylaws requires a two-thirds vote to raise or appropriate money at a special town meeting and argued that transfers should be treated similarly.

public_comment.speaker: John Bowen
public_comment.topic: Athletics expenditures and funding by participants and families
public_comment.quote: citing state end-of-year reports, he stated that athletics expenditures increased from approximately $358,000 in fy2017 to approximately $575,000 in fy2025 while the share covered by athletic fees declined.
